official.deadline_note: The bursary page states applications are submitted twice a year, by 31 March and 31 October of the calendar year; Rector's Directive No. 56/2025 describes the period as annual from 31 March to 31 October. Applications go through the Dean to the Chair of the Bursary Board, so allow time for faculty processing before the cut-off.
official.application_cycle: 2026/2027 academic year, twice-yearly rounds closing 31 March and 31 October
official.status_note: The bursary page (last changed 1 September 2026) states that applications are submitted twice a year by 31 March and 31 October, so the round closing 31 October 2026 is the one currently open.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The bursary is a monthly cash payment from Charles University; no tuition coverage is published anywhere on the bursary page or in Rector's Directive No. 56/2025.
benefits: Monthly bursary of up to CZK 5,000 paid by the University Rectorate to the holder's account by the 15th day of each month, including during holidays
A separate contribution towards living expenses may be requested as part of preparation for studies in the Czech language
The bursary may be held for the standard period of study in the enrolled programme
eligibility: International student whose studies are hindered or prevented by repression under totalitarian, authoritarian or other non-democratic regimes anywhere in the world
From a country where, according to humanitarian organisations, human rights and freedoms are being violated and discriminatory measures restrict access to education
Already admitted and enrolled in a degree programme at a Charles University faculty through the standard admissions procedure

Participants in the Czech Studies lifelong learning programme at the Faculty of Arts or at the Institute for Language and Preparatory Studies, and applicants for study at the University, may also submit through the dean
requirements: Be directly affected by coming from a country where, in the assessment of generally respected humanitarian organisations, human rights and freedoms are constantly violated and the state exposes persons to oppression, harassment or repression resulting in discriminatory measures in relation to receiving education
Complete the application form published on the University website
Provide all required documents under Article 2, point 3 of Rector's Directive No. 56/2025
Submit documents proving persecution in English, or with a certified Czech translation if they are in less commonly used foreign languages
By 31 October of each academic year, confirm the amount of any other financial support for education, or submit an affirmation that none is received
documents: Completed application form available on the Charles University website
Documents proving compliance with the eligibility condition under Article 2, paragraph 2
Personal letter to the Bursary Board
Transcript of study results achieved to date
Confirmation of the amount of other financial support for education, or an affirmation proving that none is received
selection_criteria: Applications are discussed and considered by the Bursary Board case by case, and the Board issues a recommendation for the Rector including the proposed amount
Applicants from the Duolingo x UNHCR Access Scholars Programme nominated by Duolingo English Test are given preference by both the Board and the Rector
The Board meets at least twice a year, immediately after the end of an application submission period
The Board may initiate withdrawal or reduction of the bursary if other financial support is received or other serious reasons arise
coverage: Monthly cash payment of up to CZK 5,000
Optional contribution towards living expenses for applicants preparing studies in the Czech language
application_method: Submit the application to the Student Affairs Office of the Charles University faculty at which the student is enrolled
Attach the application form and all documents required under Article 2, point 3 of Rector's Directive No. 56/2025
The faculty forwards the complete application digitally, via the Dean or an authorised Vice-Dean, to the Chair of the Václav Havel Bursary Board
The Board recommends and the Rector decides on the award and its amount
official.application_route: File with your own faculty's Student Affairs Office; the Dean forwards the file digitally to the Chair of the Václav Havel Bursary Board, and the Rector decides.
official.study_mode: Full-time or part-time study at a Charles University faculty, for the standard period of study
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality restriction is published; eligibility is based on repression of the applicant and their country situation rather than on citizenship.
official.international_eligibility: The bursary is intended for international students; students already admitted and enrolled at a Charles University faculty through the standard admissions procedure.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Any degree programme at a Charles University faculty; participates also include the Czech Studies lifelong learning programme at the Faculty of Arts and programmes of the Institute for Language and Preparatory Studies.
official.duration: Standard period of study in the programme in which the holder is enrolled, or the duration of participation in a lifelong learning programme
official.description: Charles University's own financial support for students of the University and participants in lifelong learning whose study is made more difficult or impossible by repression by totalitarian, authoritarian or non-free regimes, giving an opportunity for education to those illegitimately denied it. It is governed by Rector's Directive No. 56/2025, effective 22 December 2025.
official.program_type: University hardship bursary governed by Rector's Directive No. 56/2025

verification.notes: Read the official Charles University bursary page and the full text of Rector's Directive No. 56/2025 (PDF); the CZK 5,000 per month maximum comes from Article 4(3) of that Directive and the twice-yearly 31 March / 31 October deadlines from the bursary page.

applicant_utility.summary: You must already be admitted and enrolled at a Charles University faculty before this bursary can be awarded, so it is not a way to fund your way in - it tops up an existing study place with up to CZK 5,000 a month. The application is filed with your own faculty's Student Affairs Office and travels digitally through the Dean to the Bursary Board, which means your faculty's paperwork speed, not just the 31 October date, decides your timetable. Nominated Duolingo x UNHCR Access Scholars get preference and only need to send the form plus a financial-support confirmation.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Students already enrolled at a Charles University faculty who can document state repression affecting their access to education and need a modest monthly top-up to keep studying.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm enrolment in a Charles University degree programme first - the bursary is only awarded to admitted and enrolled students
Collect documents proving persecution and translate anything in a less commonly used language into Czech with a certified translator
Write the personal letter to the Board explaining your own, direct exposure to repression and its effect on your studies
Get a transcript of results achieved to date from your faculty
Prepare either proof of other education funding or a signed affirmation that you receive none, and remember to reconfirm every year by 31 October
common_rejection_risks: Applying before being admitted and enrolled, when the award cannot legally be made
Persecution documents left in a language the Board cannot read without a certified Czech translation
A CV-heavy file with no personal letter to the Board, which the Directive lists as a separate mandatory item
Failing to report other funding received during the year, which the Board treats as grounds to reduce or withdraw the award
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees, accommodation, food and all other living costs beyond the up-to-CZK 5,000 monthly bursary; the optional living-expense contribution for Czech-language preparation has no published amount.
document_audit: Article 2 point 3 lists six separate items and the file is processed through your faculty, so a missing item stalls the whole submission
Persecution documents may be in English but anything in less commonly used languages needs a certified Czech translation
The financial-support document is required even if the answer is none - you must supply an affirmation
If you are a Duolingo x UNHCR nominee only the form and the financial-support document are required, so do not send the full set unnecessarily
alerts: The round closing 31 October 2026 is still open; the next is 31 March 2027
The bursary is capped at CZK 5,000 per month, and the Rector may set a lower amount on the Board's recommendation
Interrupting study or exceeding the standard period of study ends entitlement
Versions approved under the earlier Directive 24/2022 are not subject to the CZK 5,000 cap, so the applicable Directive depends on when you were awarded
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Faculty Student Affairs Office, then the Dean or an authorised Vice-Dean, then the Chair of the Bursary Board for a case-by-case review and a recommendation to the Rector, who fixes the amount.
